findings.claim: The change still commits non-allow-listed "Charcoal Agent" and "Lovable" naming references despite the repo-hygiene criterion requiring the repo-wide grep to find none outside the D-005 allow-list.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 3.3 requires "the repo-wide grep finds no product-name \"Charcoal\"/Lovable references outside the D-005 allow-list"; this added file says "Charcoal Agent" and "Lovable URL" on line 3, and line 11 also says `remove "Charcoal Agent"` and `Lovable boilerplate`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove/reword these references from committed OpenSpec docs or explicitly extend the D-005 allow-list and the naming guard to cover intentional historical references.

findings.claim: The standalone wordmark does not reliably expose the required accessible name because it puts `aria-label` on a generic span while hiding all text children from assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 1.1 requires brand components with accessible name "KnowMe"; `KnowMeWordmark` renders a plain `<span>` with `aria-label={decorative ? undefined : "KnowMe"}` and both visible child spans have `aria-hidden="true"`.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the standalone wordmark an appropriate semantic role such as `role="img"` when not decorative, or stop hiding the child text and use visually contiguous text that assistive tech can read as KnowMe.

findings.claim: Removing the `mode === "development" && componentTagger()` plugin leaves the `mode` parameter unused, risking an ESLint failure despite the verification claim of a clean lint run.
findings.evidence: The vite config hunk removes `import { componentTagger } from "lovable-tagger";` and changes `plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), mode === "development" && componentTagger()].filter(Boolean)` to `plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()]`, eliminating the shown use of `mode`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `mode` from the `defineConfig` callback destructuring, or rename it to an ignored parameter if the lint config allows that.
